# A signed normal increment generated by the existing compact receiver

8 September 2026. New bounded calculation for the **same actual unforced
solution** \(Q_h\), starting from its existing original datum. The source
is the compact receiver's own envelope stress, projected by the full
periodic Leray operator. No donor or force is added. The conclusion is a
signed normal nonlinear increment at frequencies coarser than that
receiver. It is not a new short-wave amplifier, an infinite cascade, or a
solution of ROOT or FORCED-D. No DNS is used.

This sharpens the mean-source observation in
[the generated-receiver note](generated-receiver.md): it
establishes a sign for a cone of modes of the **complete actual initial
nonlinear source**, then follows that sign over an explicit short time.
It does not identify those modes with a later outgoing polarization.

## 1. Statement and Fourier convention

Keep the same data and choices as the
[logarithmic-host theorem](../navier-stokes/logarithmic-host.md), with
\(\eta>0\) fixed sufficiently small as there. Put

\[
 q_0=V_j+Z_{1,h}(0),\qquad z_0=Z_{2,h}(0),\qquad
 Q_h(0)=q_0+z_0,\quad k=h^{3/2},\quad d=h^{5/4}.
\]

Let \(x_0=Y_h(0)\), let \(b_c(0)\) and \(\xi_c(0)\) be the already
prepared receiving amplitude and covector, and define

\[
 a_h=|b_c(0)|\asymp k\ell^{-13/8},\qquad
 e_b=b_c(0)/a_h,\qquad e_n=\xi_c(0)/|\xi_c(0)|.
                                                               \tag{1}
\]

Thus \(e_b\perp e_n\). The vector \(e_n\) is the **original** receiving
phase normal. It is not the normal of the outgoing wave at \(t_\eta\).
The vectors and \(a_h\) can depend on \(h\); they are not new inputs.

Choose a sufficiently large but fixed initial-data majorant
\(\mathcal E_h=\ell^A\exp(B\ell)\), with \(A,B>0\) fixed below, and
set

\[
 \kappa_h=d^{-1}\mathcal E_h^{-2}=h^{-5/4+o(1)},
 \qquad \tau_h=h^7.                                  \tag{2}
\]

The domain has side \(2\pi L\), \(L=h^{-10}\), and physical rescaled
Fourier frequencies are \(K\in L^{-1}\mathbb Z^3\). To avoid hiding its
volume, use the **unnormalized** coefficient

\[
 \widetilde v(K)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}v(x)e^{-iK\cdot x}\,dx.
                                                               \tag{3}
\]

There is a cone-annulus \(\mathcal C_h\), of fixed positive relative
volume and opening, with \(\kappa_h\le|K|\le2\kappa_h\) and
\(K\cdot e_b,K\cdot e_n\ge c\kappa_h\), such that for every lattice
frequency in that cone and all sufficiently small \(h\),

\[
 \operatorname{Im}\left[
 e^{iK\cdot x_0}e_n\cdot\widetilde{
       -\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(Q_h(0)\otimes Q_h(0))}(K)
 \right]\ge c\kappa_h a_h^2d^3.                     \tag{4}
\]

Its sign persists in the actual nonlinear Duhamel increment:

\[
 \operatorname{Im}\left[e^{iK\cdot x_0}e_n\cdot
 \left(\widetilde Q_h(\tau_h,K)
  -e^{-\epsilon|K|^2\tau_h}\widetilde Q_h(0,K)\right)\right]
       \ge c\tau_h\kappa_h a_h^2d^3.                 \tag{5}
\]

The right side in (5) is of order
\(h^{25/2}\ell^{-13/4}\mathcal E_h^{-2}\), up to fixed constants.
The normalized Fourier coefficient is (5) divided by \((2\pi L)^3\).
Smooth compact data already have Fourier tails, so (5) is deliberately
relative to the heat evolution of the **complete same initial datum**;
it does not assert an initially zero mode.

The cone may also be chosen a fixed angle away from the plane spanned by
the two original central fast covectors. This is an independently directed
Fourier increment. It does not establish a third geometrical-optics phase:
\(\kappa_h\ll k^{-1}\), while \(\kappa_h\gg h^{-1}\).

## 2. The existing original receiver and its stress mass

At time zero the central heat clock vanishes. The exact general-profile
curl lift in the full-profile theorem has the form

\[
 z_0=-b(x)F(S(x)/k)-k c(x)\mathcal Q(S(x)/k),
 \quad c=\operatorname{curl}_x\left[-\frac{\xi\times b}{|\xi|^2}\right],
 \quad \mathcal Q_s=F,\quad \langle\mathcal Q\rangle=0.
                                                               \tag{6}
\]

An overall simultaneous sign change has no effect on the stress.
The fixed \(F\) is odd, real, periodic, and nonzero; \(\mathcal Q\) is
even. The original datum contains the **complete** curl term in (6).
In particular \(z_0\) is exactly solenoidal.

Write its transported bump at zero as \(\chi_0\). Incompressibility of
the already known first-stage preparation gives

\[
 \int\chi_0^2dx=d^3\int\chi^2dx,\qquad
 \operatorname{diam}(\operatorname{supp}\chi_0)
               \le d\mathcal E_h.
                                                               \tag{7}
\]

The original central-to-envelope estimates, with the small central
normalization in (1) retained, imply

\[
 b(x)=a_h\chi_0(x)[e_b+o(1)]
\]

uniformly after factoring out \(\chi_0\). The relative error is bounded
by \(h^\sigma\mathcal E_h\) for some fixed \(\sigma>0\), after
enlarging the majorant. Indeed the source bounds give an absolute
unweighted error \((d/h)\exp(C\ell)\); division by the nonzero central
factor of order \(\ell^{-5/2}\) costs only a fixed power of \(\ell\).
The inverse and direct covector estimates obey the same finite-order
majorants. Through the orders used below, derivatives of the initial
profiles cost at most \(d^{-1}\mathcal E_h\) per derivative, and
\(|\xi|\asymp\ell\) on the support.

The exact phase-mean stress of (6) is

\[
 T_0(x)=\langle F^2\rangle b\otimes b
        +k^2\langle\mathcal Q^2\rangle c\otimes c.     \tag{8}
\]

The mixed terms vanish because \(\langle F\mathcal Q\rangle=0\).
The curl contribution has integral at most
\(a_h^2d^3(k/d)^2\mathcal E_h=o(a_h^2d^3)\), with a larger fixed
majorant allowed. Consequently

\[
 \int T_0(x)dx=M_h e_b\otimes e_b+o(M_h),\qquad
 M_h=\langle F^2\rangle\left(\int\chi^2\right)a_h^2d^3>0.
                                                               \tag{9}
\]

This positivity comes from the actual prescribed nonnegative energy
density. It requires neither a radial bump nor a special symmetry of its
center. By (7) and \(|K|\le2\kappa_h\),

\[
 e^{iK\cdot x_0}\widetilde T_0(K)
       =M_h e_b\otimes e_b+o(M_h)                     \tag{10}
\]

uniformly on the stated annulus. The extra Fourier error is at most
\(C|K|d\mathcal E_h M_h\le C\mathcal E_h^{-1}M_h\).
All choices of the fixed constants in \(\mathcal E_h\) are made before
taking \(h\) small.

## 3. Every other part of the initial stress is smaller in this band

Equation (10) alone is a phase-mean statement. To use it for the actual
initial NS source, decompose the exact stress as

\[
 Q_h(0)\otimes Q_h(0)=T_0+
 [z_0\otimes z_0-T_0]+q_0\otimes z_0+z_0\otimes q_0+q_0\otimes q_0.
                                                               \tag{11}
\]

Every term in the square brackets, and every receiver factor in the
mixed stresses, has nonzero phase Fourier index. If that index is \(n\),
its spatial phase is \(nS/k-K\cdot x\). On the support,

\[
 |n\xi/k-K|\ge c|n|\ell/k
\]

because \(\kappa_h k/\ell\to0\). Repeated integration by parts with
the gradient of this full phase has no stationary point. Twelve
integrations suffice. The curl term needs at most thirteen primary slow
derivatives; the existing C18/C24 and fixed profile A80 budget covers
them. Derivatives of the slowly varying \(q_0\) cost \(h^{-1}\), which
is smaller than \(d^{-1}\). The compact support is \(O(d^3)\), including
its possible anisotropy. Thus, with fixed subpower factors suppressed,

\[
 \left|\widetilde{z_0\otimes z_0-T_0}(K)\right|
       \le a_h^2d^3(k/d)^{12}h^{-o(1)},
\]
\[
 \left|\widetilde{q_0\otimes z_0+z_0\otimes q_0}(K)\right|
       \le a_hd^3(k/d)^{12}h^{-o(1)}
       =h^{33/4-o(1)}.                               \tag{12}
\]

The extra factor \(1/a_h\) in comparing the mixed stress to \(M_h\)
is explicitly paid: the ratio is \(h^{3/2-o(1)}\), rather than simply
\((k/d)^{12}\). Division by \(|n|\) in integration by parts and the
fixed Fourier norms justify summing all nonzero phase indices.

For the last stress in (11), use its explicit original data rather than
a late-time generic Sobolev norm. The first packet has amplitude
\(h/\ell\), support radius \(h^{1/2}\), and frequency \(O(h^{-1})\).
Its full initial curl correction is smaller by \(h/h^{1/2}=h^{1/2}\);
fixed further derivatives cost at most the same \(h^{-1}\) carrier
factor, so it is included in the following bound.
The fixed compact profile \(V_j\) has finite derivatives of every fixed
order. Twenty-four derivatives of \(q_0\otimes q_0\) in L1 therefore
cost at most

\[
 C_{24}[1+h^{5/2-24}\ell^{-1}+h^{7/2-24}\ell^{-2}].
\]

Since \(|K|\asymp h^{-5/4}\mathcal E_h^{-2}\), its Fourier tail obeys

\[
 |\widetilde{q_0\otimes q_0}(K)|
          \le h^{17/2-o(1)}=o(M_h).                  \tag{13}
\]

The first-stage original datum has these fixed derivatives; no actual
late-time Q derivative is being inferred from a C1 error. Meanwhile
\(M_h\asymp h^{27/4}\ell^{-13/4}\). Equations (10)–(13) give the
complete initial stress coefficient

\[
 e^{iK\cdot x_0}\widetilde{Q_h(0)\otimes Q_h(0)}(K)
           =M_h e_b\otimes e_b+o(M_h).               \tag{14}
\]

## 4. The signed normal source includes the full pressure

For every nonzero periodic Fourier frequency the exact NS nonlinear
source is

\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal N}(K)
       =-i\Pi_K\widetilde{Q_h\otimes Q_h}(K)K,
 \qquad \Pi_K=I-K\otimes K/|K|^2.                    \tag{15}
\]

This formula includes both ordered mixed products and the entire periodic
pressure. Because \(e_n\cdot e_b=0\), (14) gives

\[
 e_n\cdot\Pi_K(M_h e_b\otimes e_b)K
       =-M_h\frac{(e_n\cdot K)(e_b\cdot K)^2}{|K|^2}.
                                                               \tag{16}
\]

For directions with both displayed components positive and bounded below
by a fixed fraction of \(|K|\), (15)–(16) prove (4). The leading normal
component is **entirely pressure-generated**: the unprojected rank-one
stress divergence has no \(e_n\) component.

There is no need to choose a new field to obtain an independent direction.
Inside that open cone, choose a smaller fixed-angle cone whose directions
stay a fixed distance from the plane of the two central fast covectors.
Such a choice is uniformly possible for every plane: either the original
cone center already has that distance or a fixed small displacement toward
the plane's normal does, while preserving positive \(e_b,e_n\) components.
The frequency lattice has spacing \(L^{-1}\ll\kappa_h\), so this cone
contains many allowed frequencies. This describes existing nonlinear
Fourier output, not an additional geometrical-optics ansatz or donor.

## 5. A signed increment in the actual trajectory

Let \(u=Q_h\). Unforced energy and the finite construction give
\(\sup_t\|u(t)\|_2\le C\). The pointwise whole-support bounds used in
the logarithmic-host theorem, together with its correction and C1 error,
give \(\sup_t\|\nabla u(t)\|_\infty\le C\ell^2\). The theorem also
gives \(\|u\|_{H^{12}}\le h^{-117/8-C_{12}B\eta-o(1)}\), with
\(C_{12}B\eta<1\). Uniform L2 Sobolev interpolation gives

\[
 \epsilon\|\Delta u\|_2
 \le C\nu h^4\|u\|_2^{5/6}\|u\|_{H^{12}}^{1/6}
 \le h^{25/16-C_{12}B\eta/6-o(1)}
 \le h^{67/48-o(1)}=o(1).                            \tag{17}
\]

The full equation, including Leray pressure with L2 operator norm one,
therefore gives

\[
 \|\partial_tu\|_2\le\epsilon\|\Delta u\|_2
                       +\|u\|_2\|\nabla u\|_\infty
              \le C\ell^2.
\]

In particular the unnormalized Fourier stress satisfies

\[
 |\widetilde{u(t)\otimes u(t)-u(0)\otimes u(0)}(K)|
 \le(\|u(t)\|_2+\|u(0)\|_2)\|u(t)-u(0)\|_2
 \le Ct\ell^2.                                       \tag{18}
\]

On \(0\le t\le\tau_h=h^7\), this is \(o(M_h)\), since
\(\tau_h\ell^2/M_h\le C h^{1/4}\ell^{21/4}\to0\).
Equation (15) and the positive margin in (4) therefore retain the same
sign and at least half its size throughout that interval. The exact
Duhamel formula is

\[
 \widetilde u(\tau_h,K)-e^{-\epsilon|K|^2\tau_h}\widetilde u(0,K)
     =\int_0^{\tau_h}e^{-\epsilon|K|^2(\tau_h-s)}
                                  \widetilde{\mathcal N}(s,K)ds.
\]

The real scalar heat factor is positive and
\(\epsilon\kappa_h^2\tau_h=O(h^{17/2}\mathcal E_h^{-4})=o(1)\).
This proves (5) for the actual unforced solution with its unchanged
initial data, not for an independently solved mean equation.

## 6. A band-sensitive size estimate and its limitations

To express the size without a single-mode volume penalty, choose a fixed
nonnegative smooth cutoff on a smaller cone-annulus, rescale it to
\(\mathcal C_h\), and average the imaginary coefficients in (5) with
weight \((2\pi L)^{-3}\). The sum of those weights is comparable to
\(\kappa_h^3\). The resulting functional has uniformly bounded
L-infinity dual norm: its kernel is a translate and periodization of a
rescaled Schwartz kernel, whose L1 norm is independent of \(\kappa_h,L\).
Thus for

\[
 w_h=Q_h(\tau_h)-e^{\epsilon\tau_h\Delta}Q_h(0),
\]

one obtains

\[
 \|e_n\cdot w_h\|_\infty
       \ge c\tau_h M_h\kappa_h^4
       \asymp h^{35/4}\ell^{-13/4}\mathcal E_h^{-8}.  \tag{19}
\]

Applying the same cutoff to the real coefficient of
\(\partial_{e_n}(e_n\cdot w_h)\), and using
\(e_n\cdot K\ge c\kappa_h\), gives

\[
 \|\partial_{e_n}(e_n\cdot w_h)\|_\infty
       \ge c\tau_h M_h\kappa_h^5
       \asymp h^{15/2}\ell^{-13/4}\mathcal E_h^{-10}. \tag{20}
\]

These are lower bounds witnessed by the selected envelope-frequency band;
they do not assert that this band dominates the full nonlinear change.
They also do not assert a coherent packet, a lower bound at the old core,
or a polarization suitable for a later handover.

In physical variables the elapsed time is \(h^{24}\tau_h=h^{31}\), the
band wavelength is \(h^{10}/\kappa_h=h^{45/4}\mathcal E_h^2\), velocity
increments acquire \(h^{-14}\), and gradients acquire \(h^{-24}\).
All norms in (4)–(20) were stated in the rescaled variables. The family
still changes its original physical datum with \(h\).

The decisive new conclusion is a signed, nonzero pressure-generated
normal increment in the existing actual flow. The remaining task is to
follow an explicitly selected part of it under the **full time-dependent
two-wave solution**, including its turning polarization, damping, spatial
localization and possible cancellations. Its frequency is lower than the
current receiver's and its present size is small. Neither (5) nor (20)
supplies a further gain or an infinite trajectory.

Exact SymPy multiplication independently checked the full projected sign
in (16). Rational arithmetic checked the stress, tail, Duhamel, filtered
velocity/gradient and viscosity powers displayed above. These are bounded
algebra controls; they do not replace the written nonstationary-phase and
actual-trajectory estimates.
